post-qftx-n2-pure-su2-ultraviolet-model.physical_scope: Independently adopted classical pure rigid N=2 SU(2) ultraviolet vector-multiplet model, no microscopic matter hypermultiplets; no constructed quantum continuum or empirical assertion.

post-qftx-n2-pure-su2-ultraviolet-model:
## Postulate

Adopt independently a rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ pure Yang–Mills model on oriented and time-oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with increasing $x^0$ time orientation and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The global group is $SU(2)$, with one supplied smooth right principal bundle $P\to M$ and smooth equivariant local trivializations. The connection and its curvature are $A$ and $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, in the right-action convention of the Yang–Mills model supplier. Use anti-Hermitian $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(XY)$; let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be its complex-bilinear extension and $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$. Fix $g>0$ dimensionless and theta angle zero. A bundle sector means its smooth equivariant isomorphism class over $M$; only the supplied sector is used.

The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty. The vector multiplet comprises the connection, one complex adjoint scalar $\phi$, and two adjoint left-Weyl fermions. In $\mathcal N=1$ packaging it is a real adjoint vector superfield $V$ and an adjoint chiral superfield $\Phi$, not a matter hypermultiplet. Use the supplied superspace derivatives, chirality, ordered Berezin measures and vector-supergauge convention, including

$$\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^2(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R}),\qquad [X]_D=-\tfrac14 I_D(X),\qquad [Y]_F=\tfrac12 I_F(Y).$$

Here $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}$ is the represented matrix curvature, not the abstract Lie-algebra curvature used in the action. With Hermitian $t_{a,R}=i\rho_{R*}(T_a)$, let $W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$ denote the canonically normalized component field-strength superfields, so $\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}=2g\,t_{a,R}W_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a$. Define the abstract connection-normalized curvature by

$$\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha}=gT_aW_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}^a,\qquad \rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\frac{\mathcal C_{\alpha,R}}{2i}.$$

In the fundamental representation, $\kappa_{\mathbb C}=-2\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}$ therefore gives $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)$, with the same ordered spinor product on both sides. This is a classical representation/component normalization, not a quantum field-rescaling or threshold-matching theorem.

Adopt the connection-normalized microscopic action

$$S_{\mathrm{pure}}=\int_M d^4x\left\{\frac1{g^2}[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi)]_D+\left(\left[\frac1{4g^2}\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}^\alpha,\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn},\alpha})\right]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $I_D,I_F$ are the raw ordered mathematical integrals, and the physical action brackets and chiral components use Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components. The Hermitian-conjugate operation applies only to the chiral F term; the D term is real. Equivalently, the fundamental matrix F integrand is $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf2}(\mathcal C^\alpha\mathcal C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$, plus its Hermitian conjugate. Its bosonic gauge density is fixed to $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g^2)$. There is no chiral superpotential, hypermultiplet, hypermultiplet mass, or FI parameter in this ultraviolet datum. The scalar is connection-normalized; its canonical version is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$. In the same local Berezin normalization the quadratic microscopic prepotential is $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=i\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi)/(2g^2)$, with positive imaginary Hessian $\kappa/g^2$. The prepotential has mass dimension two. The dimensions are $[x]=-1$, $[\theta]=-1/2$, $[A]=[\phi]=1$, $[F_A]=2$, $[\mathcal W_{\mathrm{conn}}]=[\mathcal C]=3/2$, and $[g]=0$.

Eight real rigid supercharges, their $\mathcal N=2$ algebra and invariance of this adopted action are model premises, not a locally proved invariance theorem. Variations are smooth and compactly supported; actions are on relatively compact regions or where integrable. A small $\mathcal N=1$ adjoint-mass perturbation and the Seiberg–Witten solution are separate subsequent inputs. In particular an emergent infrared monopole hypermultiplet is not microscopic matter added to this pure model. This postulate defines classical ultraviolet field/action data; it constructs no quantum measure, regulator limit, interacting continuum theory, or empirical verification.

def-qftx-susy-vacuum-moduli-data.physical_scope: A definition of classical flat vacua for a finite-dimensional canonical rigid supersymmetric gauge model and a conditional definition of quantum vacuum sectors when a full Hilbert-space theory has been constructed; it asserts no continuum construction or relation between the two sets.

def-qftx-susy-vacuum-moduli-data:
## Definition

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ in four-dimensional rigid, global
$\mathcal N=1$ gauge-model data. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex
Hermitian vector space of scalar field values, let a compact Lie group $G$ act
unitarily on $V$, and fix an orthonormal complex basis
$(\phi^1,\ldots,\phi^n)$ of $V$. Choose Hermitian matrices
$T_a$ for the infinitesimal action of a basis of the Lie algebra of $G$, a
gauge coupling $g>0$, and a gauge-invariant holomorphic polynomial
$W:V\to\mathbb C$. Assume canonical scalar kinetic energy and no
Fayet--Iliopoulos term. Define the auxiliary-field maps

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\sum_i\partial_\mu\overline{\phi^i}\,\partial^\mu\phi^i,\qquad [\phi^i]=\mathrm{mass},\quad [W]=\mathrm{mass}^3,\quad [g]=1.$$

$$F_i(\phi)=\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi^i}(\phi),\qquad D_a(\phi)=-g\,\phi^\dagger T_a\phi.$$

The tree-level scalar potential is

$$V_{\mathrm{tree}}(\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n|F_i(\phi)|^2+\frac12\sum_a D_a(\phi)^2.$$

Thus $F_i$ and $D_a$ have mass dimension two and $V_{\mathrm{tree}}$ has
mass dimension four.

A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar
configuration $\phi\in V$ for which every $F_i(\phi)$ and every
$D_a(\phi)$ is zero. Its **classical vacuum-moduli set** is the topological
orbit space

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{\phi\in V:F_i(\phi)=0\text{ for all }i,\ D_a(\phi)=0\text{ for all }a\}/G.$$

where two configurations are identified exactly when they lie in the same
compact-$G$ orbit, and the set has the quotient topology. The stability
convention here retains every such compact-group orbit, including singular
orbits. No quotient by the complexified group, geometric-invariant-theory
stability criterion, or smooth-manifold structure is included in this
definition.

For a **specified, already constructed quantum theory** $\mathcal T$, suppose
there is a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary translation representation
$U(a)$, and densely defined supercharges $Q^I$ and their Hilbert adjoints on a
common domain $\mathcal D$. A **quantum supersymmetric vacuum ray** is the
phase-equivalence class $[\Omega]$ of a normalized vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$
satisfying
$U(a)\Omega=\Omega$ for every spacetime translation $a$ and
$Q^I\Omega=(Q^I)^*\Omega=0$ for every supercharge $I$. The **quantum
vacuum-moduli set** $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$ is the set of these
rays, with the topology, if any, supplied by the constructed theory. This
definition is conditional on normalizable invariant vacuum vectors and a
specified quantum Hilbert-space model. It asserts no path-integral measure,
continuum limit, nonperturbative existence, or equality between
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$.

def-qftx-n2-coulomb-branch-data.physical_scope: A data definition for the pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) Yang–Mills Coulomb branch and its local two-derivative abelian description; the definition makes no claim that an interacting continuum theory exists or that a charge label is realized by a stable state.

def-qftx-n2-coulomb-branch-data:
## Definition

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a selected pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills model whose global gauge group is $SU(2)$.
The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty, as explicitly adopted in the independent pure-model postulate. In $\mathcal N=1$ language the gauge sector is one vector superfield and one adjoint chiral superfield with scalar $\phi\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, connection normalization $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$, positive dimensionless gauge coupling $g$, zero chiral superpotential and no ultraviolet matter mass. The low-energy charged monopole fields introduced later are emergent infrared fields, not an ultraviolet hypermultiplet. This is the selected physical datum, not a specialization inferred from the different one-hypermultiplet postulate.

A **classical Coulomb-branch configuration** is a constant adjoint scalar
configuration satisfying the model's zero auxiliary-field conditions, taken
modulo the compact $SU(2)$ gauge action. This uses the compact-group orbit
quotient in the preceding vacuum-moduli definition; it does not replace that
quotient by a complexified-group stability construction. In the
weak-coupling semiclassical frame, let $a$ be the eigenvalue coordinate fixed
by $\phi=\tfrac12\operatorname{diag}(a,-a)$, of mass dimension one. When a quantum
theory with a vacuum-moduli set has actually been constructed, the **quantum
Coulomb-branch coordinate** $u$ denotes the chosen gauge-invariant chiral
quadratic-operator expectation value in the source trace normalization for
which the weak-coupling relation is $u=a^2/2$. Its mass dimension is two.
This definition does not assert that $u$ globally parameterizes the quantum
vacua.

On an open patch $U$ of the $u$-plane where the period functions are
holomorphic and the local gauge-coupling matrix has positive imaginary part,
an **electric/magnetic frame** means a chosen ordered basis of the formal
charge lattice that fixes local cycle representatives. Their period
functions are the complex electric coordinate $a:U\to\mathbb C$ and complex
dual coordinate $a_D:U\to\mathbb C$, both of mass dimension one. The local
two-derivative abelian gauge action is encoded by a holomorphic
**prepotential** $\mathcal F_U(a)$ of mass dimension two, defined on that
patch by

$$a_D=\frac{\partial\mathcal F_U}{\partial a},\qquad \tau=\frac{\partial a_D}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial^2\mathcal F_U}{\partial a^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0.$$

The dimensionless $\tau$ is the local complexified gauge coupling; changing
the electric/magnetic frame changes the pair $(a_D,a)$ by the corresponding
integral linear transformation and may require a different local
prepotential. Thus neither period is asserted to be a single-valued global
function on a punctured branch.

For this source-normalized data, define the **formal electric/magnetic charge
label lattice** to be $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with a label
$(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The pair labels
the central-charge formula; the lattice definition does not assert that every
label is an allowed line operator, a dynamical particle, a stable state, or a
state in any constructed Hilbert space. Those are separate model data.

The word **exact** in this page refers only to the adopted source-proposed
Wilsonian two-derivative low-energy data on a regular patch of the selected
pure SU(2) model. It does not mean a proof of a nonperturbative continuum
path integral, a global single-valued prepotential, or an exact statement
about arbitrary $\mathcal N=2$ theories.

def-qftx-n2-monopole-local-dual-higgs-mo.physical_scope: Explicit constant-positive-vector-metric, two-derivative dual U(1) effective model near one pure-SU(2) N=2 monopole singularity after small N=1 mass perturbation; source superpotential retained, metric freezing and any linear-u truncation are additional approximations, with no global action, continuum construction or vortex existence asserted.

def-qftx-n2-monopole-local-dual-higgs-mo:
## Definition

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local duality frame near one
monopole singularity of the selected pure $SU(2)$, four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ model. Let $A_D$ be the complex scalar coordinate in the
local dual $U(1)_D$ vector multiplet, and let $M,\widetilde M$ be complex
scalar fields of dual electric charges $+1$ and $-1$ in two $\mathcal N=1$
chiral multiplets. These are emergent infrared monopole fields in a dual frame of the independent pure ultraviolet model, not microscopic matter hypermultiplets. The dual gauge group acts by

$$A_D\mapsto A_D,\qquad M\mapsto e^{i\alpha}M,\qquad \widetilde M\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde M,\qquad \alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z).$$

Let $u(A_D)$ be the supplied holomorphic coordinate function on an open
patch $|A_D|<r$ about $A_D=0$, with $u(0)=u_m$ and
$c:=u'(0)\ne0$. Let $\mu\ne0$ be the coefficient of the small adjoint
mass perturbation, let $g_D>0$ be the dimensionless dual gauge coupling,
and use connection normalization for $A_D$, canonical kinetic terms for $M,\widetilde M$, and zero microscopic D-type Fayet--Iliopoulos parameter. Freeze the positive local vector-multiplet metric at $b=g_D^{-2}$; this is a specified constant-coupling two-derivative approximation within the patch, not the full field-dependent Wilsonian metric.
Define

$$W_\mu(A_D,M,\widetilde M)=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D),\qquad D=g_D\bigl(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2\bigr).$$

$$V_\mu=g_D^2|\partial_{A_D}W_\mu|^2+|\partial_M W_\mu|^2+|\partial_{\widetilde M}W_\mu|^2+\frac12D^2.$$

Let $\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu\widetilde A_\nu-
\partial_\nu\widetilde A_\mu$ and
$\widetilde D_\mu A_D=\partial_\mu A_D$,
$\widetilde D_\mu M=(\partial_\mu-i\widetilde A_\mu)M$, and
$\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M=(\partial_\mu+i\widetilde A_\mu)
\widetilde M$. In metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the
connection-normalized bosonic kinetic Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\eta^{\mu\nu}\left(g_D^{-2}\partial_\mu\overline{A_D}\,\partial_\nu A_D+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu M}\,\widetilde D_\nu M+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M}\,\widetilde D_\nu\widetilde M\right)-\frac{1}{4g_D^2}\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}\widetilde F^{\mu\nu}.$$

The mass dimensions are
$[A_D]=[M]=[\widetilde M]=[\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[u]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, $[W_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}^3$,
$[F_{A_D}]=[F_M]=[F_{\widetilde M}]=[D]=[\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$,
$[\widetilde A_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[c]=\mathrm{mass}$, and $[g_D]=1$. The allowed regime is restricted to
field values within this patch and energies below its stated effective
cutoff; “small $\mu$” means that the induced scale
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ lies well below that cutoff.

For a controlled leading linear-superpotential truncation, explicitly replace $u(A_D)$ by $u_m+cA_D$ in this constant-metric model. Then the perturbation is an $F$-type FI deformation of the local $\mathcal N=2$ abelian theory, related to a D-type FI deformation by rotation of its auxiliary triplet. This extra truncation admits the critical BPS square completion. The generic holomorphic $u(A_D)$ model above is softly broken to $\mathcal N=1$ and is not asserted to have exact BPS vortices; the full physical solution and a globally valid metric are separate inputs. Neither a small $\mu$ nor a holomorphic superpotential theorem alone controls all non-holomorphic metric or higher-derivative corrections.

This is a one-singularity effective data package. It includes neither a
simultaneously local electric description of mutually nonlocal dyons nor a
claim that the local action extends over the full moduli space. A finite-energy
vortex is not part of this Definition; its existence, when needed, is a
separate hypothesis.

def-qftx-n2-dual-higgs-flux-tube-sector.physical_scope: A conditional definition of nonzero-winding, finite-energy static flux-tube profiles in the local dual U(1) Higgs model; it asserts neither existence nor stability of such profiles.

def-qftx-n2-dual-higgs-flux-tube-sector:
## Definition

Use the dual $U(1)_D$ fields and potential of the preceding local
monopole-Higgs model. Let $x^1,x^2$ be coordinates on the transverse plane
$\mathbb R^2$ and let $x^3$ be the coordinate along a straight static tube.
Write $\widetilde A_i$ for the spatial dual gauge potential,
$\widetilde F_{12}=\partial_1\widetilde A_2-\partial_2\widetilde A_1$,
$D_iM=(\partial_i-i\widetilde A_i)M$, and
$D_i\widetilde M=(\partial_i+i\widetilde A_i)\widetilde M$.

A **finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding $n$** is a smooth static
configuration $(A_D,M,\widetilde M,\widetilde A_1,\widetilde A_2)$ on
$\mathbb R^2$ for which the transverse energy

$$\sigma=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{\widetilde F_{12}^2}{2g_D^2}+g_D^{-2}|\partial_i A_D|^2+|D_iM|^2+|D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_\mu-V_{\mathrm{vac}}\right)\,d^2x$$

is finite. The fields approach a supersymmetric vacuum at infinity satisfying
$A_D=0$, $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v>0$,
$\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(0)=0$, and
$V_{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. The phase map $M/|M|$ restricted to a sufficiently
large circle has degree $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ as a map to the unit
circle; the phase map $\widetilde M/|\widetilde M|$ has degree $-n$.
Require also that $D_iM$ and $D_i\widetilde M$ tend to zero on that circle,
that the coefficient of $d\theta$ in the pulled-back one-form $\widetilde A-d\arg M$ tends uniformly in
$\theta$ to zero as the circle radius tends to infinity, and that the
limiting flux exists. The profile is a translation-invariant
tube along $x^3$; its tension is the transverse integral $\sigma$. This
Definition includes no assertion that such a configuration exists or is a
stationary solution of the field equations.

In the adopted electric/magnetic frame, the **original electric flux** of
this sector means the dual magnetic flux
$\Phi_D=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x$.
The flux dictionary is part of the selected duality model; this Definition
does not state that every electric line charge is represented by a vortex.
In natural units, $[\widetilde A_i]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[\widetilde F_{12}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, and
$[\sigma]=\mathrm{mass}^2$.

post-qftx-n2-seiberg-witten-effective-so.physical_scope: Adopted source-proposed two-derivative Wilsonian solution data for pure four-dimensional rigid N=2 SU(2) Yang–Mills, with the source's specified singularity ansatz and one local monopole patch; this is not a construction of a UV continuum QFT or a universal duality claim.

post-qftx-n2-seiberg-witten-effective-so:
## Postulate

Adopt the source-proposed low-energy solution data for pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills with global gauge group $SU(2)$, one
adjoint vector multiplet, rank one, no matter hypermultiplets, and the coupling, units, connection-normalized scalar, and prepotential convention of the independent pure ultraviolet vector-multiplet datum. Use natural units
$c=\hbar=1$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a positive
dynamical scale $\Lambda$ of mass dimension one. The gauge-invariant
coordinate $u$ has mass dimension two; set $w=u/\Lambda^2$.

The absence of microscopic hypermultiplets is an explicit model input in that independent ultraviolet postulate. The charged monopole hypermultiplet in a local infrared frame below is emergent; it does not change the ultraviolet matter content.

On the regular $w$-plane with singular values $w=1,-1,\infty$ removed,
adopt the family of genus-one curves, where $x,y,w$ are dimensionless:

$$\Sigma_w:\quad y^2=(x-1)(x+1)(x-w).$$

and the meromorphic period differential

$$\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}=\frac{\sqrt2\Lambda}{2\pi}\frac{y\,dx}{x^2-1}.$$

Within this proposed solution, take the quantum vacuum-moduli data to be the
entire $u$-plane, with a $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry $u\mapsto-u$ and singular
values $u=\Lambda^2,-\Lambda^2,\infty$. This is part of the adopted
solution ansatz, not a consequence of a constructed continuum theory.

For a chosen local cycle basis $\gamma_m,\gamma_e$ on $\Sigma_w$ with
intersection number $\gamma_m\cdot\gamma_e=1$, define
$a_D=\oint_{\gamma_m}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and
$a=\oint_{\gamma_e}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$. These periods have mass
dimension one, are multivalued under continuation around the punctures, and
are used in the local prepotential convention
$a_D=\partial\mathcal F/\partial a$ and
$\tau=\partial^2\mathcal F/\partial a^2$ with
$\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. In the source's counterclockwise-loop
convention, the period column $(a_D,a)^T$ has monodromy matrices

$$M_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_-=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}.$$

Adopt the source's formal charge-label lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and central-charge pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}=n_ea+n_ma_D$ for labels
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. In the supersymmetry convention of this page,
the scalar central charge is normalized as
$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}$. The mass inequality and its
saturation statement are separate theorem deductions. No claim is made that
every lattice label is an allowed line operator or is represented by a stable
particle.

Adopt the singularity interpretation that the $w=1$ point has a light
monopole with $a_D=0$, while the $w=-1$ point has a light dyon with
$a-a_D=0$ in the chosen frame. These are source-proposed physical inputs
tested by their monodromies; they are not deduced here from a constructed
continuum theory.
In the local monopole patch, adopt the dual $U(1)_D$ field content and superpotential described in the preceding effective-model definition. The source two-derivative vector metric is positive and generally field dependent, determined by the local dual coupling; a regulated matching scale is part of any effective action with the light monopole retained. That definition explicitly freezes this metric at $b=g_D^{-2}>0$ for the subsequent classical calculations. Metric freezing, and the further replacement of $u(A_D)$ by its linear Taylor term where explicitly requested, are additional approximations, not exact identities of the full period solution. No bound on their discarded corrections is adopted here. A small N=1-breaking mass parameter $\mu$ of
mass dimension one adds the local superpotential term $\mu u(A_D)$ to
$\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M$. The local description applies only near this
singularity, below its effective cutoff, and does not simultaneously describe
the mutually nonlocal dyon at the other singularity.

Here **exact low-energy solution** means the adopted two-derivative
Wilsonian data of this source-defined model on its regular patches. It does
not mean a proof of a nonperturbative UV path integral, a global
single-valued prepotential, or an identity for arbitrary gauge groups,
matter contents, or N=2 theories.

pthm-qftx-n2-bps-central-charge-mass.physical_scope: Conditional representation-theoretic mass bound for an existing massive state in a selected pure-SU(2) N=2 Seiberg–Witten period patch; it asserts neither state existence nor stability, and does not construct the underlying continuum QFT.

pthm-qftx-n2-bps-central-charge-mass:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Use the four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ super-Poincare convention
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\epsilon_{12}=1$, and
$c=\hbar=1$. Let $U$ be a regular patch of the selected pure-SU(2)
Seiberg--Witten period data. Fix $u\in U$ and a formal charge label
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. Suppose the selected physical model has a
nonzero massive unitary rest-fiber representation $\mathcal K$ with mass
$M>0$, scalar central-charge matrix $Z^{12}=zI$, $Z^{21}=-zI$, a common
dense invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, and actual Hilbert adjoints for
all supercharges. Require its charge normalization to be

$$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2\bigl(n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)\bigr).$$

Then

$$M\ge\sqrt2\,|n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)|.$$

If equality holds, then $|z|=M>0$; set $\omega=z/|z|$, so
$|\omega|=1$ and $\overline\omega z=|z|$, and define
$A=Q^1_1-\omega(Q^2_2)^*$ and
$A^\sharp=(Q^1_1)^*-\overline\omegaQ^2_2$ on $\mathcal D$. Both
$A\psi$ and $A^\sharp\psi$ vanish for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$.
Equality defines algebraic BPS saturation only; the statement asserts no
state exists for any chosen charge label and no BPS state is stable.

pthm-qftx-n2-dual-higgs-vortex-flux-and-.physical_scope: Conditional classical result for an already existing smooth nonzero-winding finite-energy vortex profile in the local dual U(1) effective model; it proves flux quantization and positive tension, not vortex existence, stability, or a confining ground-state potential.

pthm-qftx-n2-dual-higgs-vortex-flux-and-:
## Statement

Use the local dual $U(1)_D$ model with natural units, positive coupling

conditions of the preceding definition. If a finite-energy dual vortex
profile of winding $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ exists, then its dual

$$\Phi_D=2\pi n,$$

and its transverse tension satisfies $0<\sigma<\infty$. This is a
conditional statement about an admitted profile; it asserts neither
existence nor stability of any vortex or a linearly confining minimum-energy
potential between external charges.

pthm-qftx-n2-monopole-condensation-after.physical_scope: Local effective-model F/D vacuum and dual Higgs mass near one pure-SU(2) monopole singularity, plus actual positive asymptotically linear nonlinear magnetostatic fixed-electric-flux energy on the explicitly bounded neutral patch. Generic infima need not be attained and no generic O(1) remainder, UV matching, quantum area law or framework-wide confinement is asserted; the separate exact critical-truncation branch retains its stronger hypotheses.

pthm-qftx-n2-monopole-condensation-after:
## Statement

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local monopole patch of the
selected pure-SU(2) N=2 source-proposed low-energy model. Let $u(A_D)$,
$c=u'(0)\ne0$, $M$, $\widetilde M$, $g_D$, and $\mu$ be the data in the
local dual-Higgs definition, with $\mu\ne0$ and
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ well below the effective cutoff. Restrict to a
neighborhood of $A_D=0$ on which $u'(A_D)\ne0$. The supersymmetric vacuum
equations in this patch have exactly one $U(1)_D$ gauge orbit, represented
by

$$A_D=0,\qquad M\widetilde M=-\frac{\mu c}{\sqrt2},\qquad |M|=|\widetilde M|=v:=\left(\frac{|\mu c|}{\sqrt2}\right)^{1/2}>0.$$

Thus the local monopole fields have nonzero gauge-fixed amplitudes and
$U(1)_D$ is fully Higgsed. With canonical charged-hypermultiplet kinetic terms in the
connection-normalized local model, the dual vector mass is

$$m_D^2=2g_D^2\bigl(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2\bigr)=4g_D^2v^2>0.$$

For an actual generic nonlinear confinement conclusion, use the precise magnetostatic flux-boundary class of the nonlinear cylinder definition, with the full $u$, a closed neutral disk on which $u'\ne0$, positive metric bounds, constant or absent theta, uniformly vacuum-approaching profiles, and fixed canonical end traces. For this energy branch assume full AC, as required by its integration suppliers. The planar energy infimum $\tau_n$ is positive and finite for every $n\ne0$, and the full static-energy infimum obeys

$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{I_n(L)}{L}=\tau_n>0.$$

This proves asymptotically linear confinement of the specified original electric flux in that classical local effective model without assuming a noncritical stationary vortex or any attained minimum. It makes no generic $O(1)$ remainder claim.

For the stronger exact-remainder conclusion, make the following additional explicit
effective-model assumption: for a fixed nonzero original electric test-charge
sector and every sufficiently large separation $L$, the minimum-energy
configuration in that sector is a straight, translation-invariant dual
vortex of nonzero winding as defined here, and its endcap energy is bounded
uniformly in $L$. If that flux-tube sector exists, its original electric
flux is quantized and its tension is positive; the corresponding potential
has $V(L)=\sigma L+O(1)$, where $O(1)$ denotes a term bounded uniformly as
$L\to\infty$. This is linear confinement only in the stated local effective
model and under the stated vortex/minimization assumption. The theorem does not assert that a generic nonlinear model has an attained vortex minimum. In the separately specified constant-metric linear truncation $u=u_m+cA_D$, assume full AC and take the actual canonical fixed-flux cylinder class defined above. The critical vortex supplier now proves existence and an absolute transverse energy minimum for **every** nonzero winding and every effective divisor of degree $|n|$, with arbitrary centres and multiplicities. Actual fixed-width full-model collars exist for any fixed smooth canonical end traces in the stated closed valid neutral disk. Hence its full static-energy infimum is $4\pi v^2|n|L+O(1)$, with an exact translation-invariant minimum for matching minimizing traces. This exact critical conclusion no longer assumes a supplied solution or endcap bound; it does not transfer BPS saturation or an $O(1)$ remainder to generic nonlinear u.

pthm-qftx-n2-linear-monopole-bps-vortex-:
## Statement

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Use the constant-metric connection-normalized dual model, explicitly in the linear truncation $u(A_D)=u_m+cA_D$, with $c\ne0$, $\mu\ne0$ and $g=g_D>0$. Put $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$, $\xi=2v^2$ and $e^{i\beta}=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v^2)$. Define charge-one fields

$$q=\frac{M+e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M}}{\sqrt2},\qquad p=\frac{M-e^{i\beta}\overline{\widetilde M}}{\sqrt2},\qquad s=|q|^2+|p|^2.$$

Let $A=\widetilde A_1dx^1+\widetilde A_2dx^2$ be smooth and real on $\mathbb R^2$, $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$, $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$ and $a=A_D$. For every smooth finite-energy profile in the uniform-vacuum winding-$n$ class, $n\ne0$, with $|q|\to\sqrt\xi$, $p,a\to0$ and limiting flux $2\pi n$, the positive-winding identity is

$$E=2\pi\xi n+\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{[B-g^2(\xi-s)]^2}{2g^2}+|(D_1+iD_2)q|^2+|(D_1+iD_2)p|^2+2g^2\xi|p|^2+g^{-2}|\partial_i a|^2+2|a|^2s\right\}d^2x.$$

The boundary current is removed along a radii subsequence furnished by finite energy and uniform bounded vacuum amplitudes; no full-circle current limit or extra exponential decay assumption is required. For negative winding conjugate the charged fields and reverse A, giving $E\ge2\pi\xi|n|=4\pi v^2|n|$.

For **every** nonzero integer n and every effective finite divisor of degree $|n|$, at arbitrary centres with arbitrary positive multiplicities, the actual planar vortex theorem supplies a smooth critical pair at $e=g$, with $(D_1+iD_2)q=0$, $B=g^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ for $n>0$ and the conjugate equations for $n<0$. Its embedding

$$a=p=0,\qquad M=q/\sqrt2,\qquad \widetilde M=e^{i\beta}\bar q/\sqrt2$$

is a stationary absolute transverse energy minimum among all the above full-model profiles with the same winding, with tension $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. This is actual existence and minimum energy, not an assumed solution. Gauge-invariant curvature and covariant gradients decay exponentially. Only the degree-zero correction relative to $n\theta$ is removed by a globally smooth gauge to obtain canonical exterior fields; the degree-changing local unwound gauge is not extended across the divisor.

For the precise classical cylinder problem, use the fixed-flux class $\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)$ of Nonlinear local dual-Higgs magnetostatic flux cylinders, specialized to this **linear** u and constant $b=g^{-2}$, with any fixed smooth canonical end profiles in one closed valid neutral disk and constant or omitted theta. For every chosen arbitrary-divisor minimizing profile above, actual smooth fixed-width finite-energy collars from both ends exist and give constants $\ell>0$, $C_0,C_1<\infty$ independent of L such that

$$T_nL\le I_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1\le T_nL+C_0+C_1\qquad(L\ge2\ell).$$

Thus $I_L=T_nL+O(1)$. Matching minimizing end traces give an exact translation-invariant minimum $T_nL$. The same estimate holds for any other stated fixed-flux boundary class which admits such collars; no unspecified probe-to-end-trace dictionary is inferred. In the special case $a=p=0$ at both ends, the mathematical critical cylinder theorem supplies the embedded collar construction directly. General full-model end profiles use the proved local magnetostatic collar construction, not an assumed endcap bound.

In linear response about the Higgs vacuum, original magnetic probes are dual electric sources for a vector of mass $m_D^2=2g^2\xi$; its unit canonical static source potential is $e^{-m_Dr}/(4\pi r)$, so that response is screened. The tube carries dual magnetic, hence original electric, flux in the adopted frame. These are classical boundary-energy statements, not a quantum Wilson-loop area law or an ultraviolet matching theorem.

For a generic nonlinear u, the same embedded fields with a=0 instead have the pointwise neutral potential derivative

$$\left.\partial_{\bar a}V_\mu\right|_{a=0}=g^2\bar\mu\,\overline{u''(0)}\bigl(\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu c\bigr).$$

If nonzero anywhere, the embedded profile is not stationary for that nonlinear model. The generic nonlinear theorem proves a positive limiting energy slope; it does not inherit exact critical BPS saturation or an $O(1)$ remainder from this theorem.

def-qftx-n2-nonlinear-magnetostatic-flux:
## Definition

Use the local monopole fields, charges and superpotential with $a=A_D$, $c=u'(0)\ne0$, $\mu\ne0$, $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$ and $\xi=2v^2$. Keep the holomorphic function $u$ nonlinear. Choose a closed disk $K_\delta=\{|a|\le\delta\}$ contained in its open valid patch with $u'(a)\ne0$ throughout. Define

$$m_*=\min_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u'(a)|>0,\qquad K=\sup_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u''(a)|<\infty.$$

Continuity, compactness and the nonzero $c$ allow such a disk. No linear Taylor replacement of $u$ is made. In the already adopted constant-metric model put $b(a)=b_0=g_D^{-2}$. More generally, the same classical energy problem may be specified with a supplied smooth real function $b$ on a neighborhood of $K_\delta$ and constants $0<b_-\le b(a)\le b_+<\infty$. This is additional explicit local Wilsonian metric data, not the vector-only logarithmically singular period metric inferred at a massless-monopole point. Let $b_0=b(0)$ and $g_0^2=b_0^{-1}$. Define

$$H=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(a),\qquad d=|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2,\qquad s=|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2,$$

$$V_b=b(a)^{-1}|H|^2+\frac{d^2}{2b(a)}+2|a|^2s.$$

Charged kinetic terms are canonical. The gauge kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$ and the neutral kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$. Work in the classical magnetostatic model with omitted or **constant** theta angle, no dynamical dual magnetic sources in the interior, static fields and $A_0=0$. No field-dependent-theta Gauss-law conclusion is included.

Fix $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ and $e^{i\beta}=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v^2)$. A planar admissible profile is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx^1+A_2dx^2$ and smooth complex fields $a,M,\widetilde M$ on $\mathbb R^2$, with $a(x)\in K_\delta$, finite energy

$$E_b=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2B^2+b(a)|\partial_i a|^2+|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_b\right\}d^2x,$$

where $i=1,2$, $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$ and $\widetilde D_i=\partial_i+iA_i$. Require **uniform** approach to the vacuum orbit at transverse infinity:

$$a\to0,\qquad |M|,|\widetilde M|\to v,\qquad M\widetilde M\to e^{i\beta}v^2.$$

This is an independent boundary hypothesis, not inferred from finite energy. Outside a compact set $M$ is nonzero and its phase has winding $n$ on each sufficiently large circle; the phase of $\widetilde M$ has winding $-n$. In the angular coordinate $\theta$, require the coefficient of $d\theta$ in $A-d\arg M$ to tend uniformly to zero, and the limiting flux to exist. Require also $D_iM,\widetilde D_i\widetilde M\to0$ uniformly, as in the admitted flux-sector data. These conditions define the gauge-invariant class $\mathcal P_n$. Gauge transformations are arbitrary smooth maps $U:\mathbb R^2\to U(1)$ acting by $M\mapsto UM$, $\widetilde M\mapsto U^{-1}\widetilde M$ and $A\mapsto A-iU^{-1}dU$; there is no added asymptotic-constant gauge restriction. A **canonical exterior representative** has $M=m e^{in\theta}$ with $m>0$ real outside a compact set.

Write

$$\tau_n=\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_b(P).$$

This notation alone asserts neither nonemptiness nor attainment. The adopted electric/magnetic dictionary identifies the dual magnetic flux with the original electric flux only for the specified test-charge/flux boundary sector.

For fixed canonical exterior representatives $P_0,P_1\in\mathcal P_n$ and $L>0$, let $\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)$ be the smooth static fields on $\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with these tangential end traces, $a\in K_\delta$, and a planar admissible winding-$n$ profile on almost every slice. The flux $2\pi n$ is thus fixed throughout the cylinder, with no flux leakage to transverse infinity or interior magnetic source. Allow $A_3$ but choose $A_3=0$ in trial collars. Define

$$E_{b,3}=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2\sum_{i<j}F_{ij}^2+b(a)\sum_{i=1}^3|\partial_i a|^2+\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2\bigr)+V_b\right\}d^2x\,dx^3,$$

and $I_n(L;P_0,P_1)=\inf_{\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)}E_{b,3}$. Competitors have finite displayed energy and the stated flux/boundary data; no stationary solution or minimizer is assumed. Any further hard field cutoff is part of a different admissible class and must be checked to admit the profiles and interpolation paths used here. This functional is the specified local classical model; no error control to a microscopic action or quantum Wilson-loop interpretation is asserted.

pthm-qftx-n2-nonlinear-local-electric-fl:
## Statement

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Use the nonlinear local magnetostatic data, class $\mathcal P_n$ and fixed-flux cylinders defined above. In particular the neutral scalar lies in the specified small closed disk, the positive smooth **light-hyper-retaining** metric has the explicit bounds $b_-,b_+$, the vacuum approach is uniform, and theta is omitted or constant. Let

$$t_*=\min\{\xi/2,m_*/\sqrt2\}>0,\qquad C_V=\max\left\{\frac{4b_+\xi^2}{m_*^2},\;6b_++\frac{2K^2}{t_*}\right\},\qquad c_V=C_V^{-1},\qquad \gamma=\min\left\{1,\frac{b_-}{b_0},2b_0c_V\right\}>0.$$

Then the full nonlinear potential and every planar profile obey

$$V_b\ge c_V(s-\xi)^2,\qquad E_b\ge\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|.$$

The class $\mathcal P_n$ is nonempty for **every** nonzero integer winding: a smooth compact-core radial test suffices, with no field equation, exact BPS profile or Taubes existence theorem assumed. Consequently

$$0<\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty.$$

Every admissible profile has a globally smooth gauge transform to a canonical exterior representative. Any two such canonical representatives admit a smooth fixed-width finite-energy interpolation collar in the same winding class; the collar keeps the neutral scalar in its convex disk. In particular, for fixed end traces $P_0,P_1$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there are finite constants $C_\varepsilon$, $\ell>0$, independent of $L$, such that for $L\ge2\ell$

$$\tau_nL\le I_n(L;P_0,P_1)\le(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon.$$

Therefore

$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{I_n(L;P_0,P_1)}{L}=\tau_n>0.$$

This is asymptotically linear classical confinement of the specified original electric flux in the stated local magnetostatic boundary model. It does not assert that the planar infimum or finite-cylinder infimum is attained, that a nonlinear stationary profile is BPS, or that $I_n(L)=\tau_nL+O(1)$. The end-collar constants may depend on the chosen $\varepsilon$-profile. Exact critical $O(1)$ bounds require the stronger critical minimizing-profile input, kept separately. No conclusion follows for arbitrary microscopic line charges, flux-changing processes, a field-dependent theta term, or a quantum Wilson-loop area law.
